# SOP-P1-L3-03 First-article inspection - Machining line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, EQ-P1-L3-CN03  
Related: ECN-2026-035, QS-PROC-04, SB-1026

Purpose
1. Define the standardized first-article inspection (FAI) process for the machining line to verify conformance of the first production piece to engineering and quality requirements prior to lot release.

Background and scope
2. This procedure applies to first articles produced on the machining line served by EQ-P1-L3-IH01, EQ-P1-L3-HP02, and EQ-P1-L3-CN03. It addresses machine and process verifications, setup checks, dimensional and function checks, and required records for FAI. Use ECN-2026-035 for engineering drawing changes, QS-PROC-04 for quality acceptance criteria, and SB-1026 for safety bulletin items that impact setup.

Preconditions
3. Prior to initiating the FAI:
   1. The production order and drawing release must be confirmed per ECN-2026-035.
   2. Equipment maintenance status must be green and any open high-priority safety items from SB-1026 must be cleared or mitigated.
   3. The tool and gauge set for the part must be verified for calibration per QS-PROC-04.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Mandatory PPE during the FAI includes safety glasses, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, and steel-toe footwear. Follow items called out in SB-1026 for any additional protective requirements specific to the operation.

Inspection team and roles
5. Assignments:
   1. Production Technician — performs setup, basic machine checks, and produces the first article.
   2. Quality Inspector — performs dimensional inspection and signs the FAI record.
   3. Process Engineer — reviews setup parameters and approves process capability notes where required.

Key setup verifications and safety checks
6. Verify machine setup and safety devices before producing the first article:
   1. Confirm guarding and interlocks are engaged per SB-1026.
   2. Verify coolant and lubrication supply is operational and meets machine manufacturer guidance.
   3. Confirm coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. Record the measured flow value on the FAI checklist.
   4. For hydraulic press components, perform bolt and fastener torque verification where specified. The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 1330 N·m. Record the torque reading and who performed the check.

First-article production
7. Produce the first article using the production tooling and the same program, feeds, and speeds intended for production. Log the program identifier and tool offsets on the FAI checklist.

Dimensional and functional inspection
8. Perform the following inspections on the first article:
   1. Critical dimensions identified on the release drawing as inspection features must be measured and recorded on the FAI report.
   2. Functional checks such as fit, assembly engagement, or movement must be performed and results documented with pass/fail indication and remarks where applicable.
   3. If measured values deviate from drawing tolerances, stop and escalate to the Process Engineer and Quality Manager immediately per QS-PROC-04.

Step rationale and examples
9. Rationale:
   1. Verifying coil cooling flow ensures thermal stability of the induction heater during billet heating and prevents coil damage.
   2. Verifying the main ram bolt torque prevents mechanical loosening and maintains press alignment and safety during forging operations.
   3. Recording actual measured values on the FAI checklist provides traceability and allows correlation of process parameters to part quality.
10. Example entries for the FAI checklist (illustrative content only; record actual measured values):
   1. Coil cooling water flow: recorded measurement and inspector initials.
   2. Main ram bolt torque: 1330 N·m recorded and inspector initials.
   3. Dimensional checks: list of feature identifiers, measured values, tolerance status, and inspector initials.

Nonconformance and disposition
11. If any FAI inspection item fails:
   1. Tag the first article as nonconforming and quarantine according to QS-PROC-04.
   2. Initiate containment and corrective action per QS-PROC-04 and reference ECN-2026-035 if the failure is design related.
   3. Document root cause, corrective action, verification plan, and sign-off before resuming production.

Records and retention
12. Documents to complete and retain:
   1. Completed FAI checklist with all measured values, signatures, and remarks.
   2. Calibrations and tool offsets used during setup, referenced per QS-PROC-04.
   3. Torque verification printout or manual log showing the main ram bolt torque check for EQ-P1-L3-HP02.
   4. Flowmeter log or readout showing coil cooling water flow for EQ-P1-L3-IH01.
   5. Nonconformance reports, if any, and closure records.
   6. All records shall be filed in the document control system and retained as required by QS-PROC-04.

Sign-off
13. Signatures required to accept the FAI:
   1. Production Technician — confirms setup and first article production.
   2. Quality Inspector — confirms dimensional and functional acceptance.
   3. Process Engineer — approves process parameters and any setup deviations.

Revision and change control
14. Any change to process parameters, tooling, or inspection criteria discovered during the FAI must be documented and submitted as an engineering change request per ECN-2026-035. Update the FAI record and reissue per document control.

Appendix
15. Related documents:
   1. ECN-2026-035
   2. QS-PROC-04
   3. SB-1026

End of procedure.
